Story name: Inspect the already-built institute onboarding flow (IADM-01)
User story: As the IADM-04 engineer, I inspect how the built IADM-01 onboarding wizard handles plan attachment, invoices/payment, and activation timing, so the PENDING-until-paid contract is based on real code.
Acceptance criteria: Report lists: where onboarding picks or stores a plan; any existing payment/invoice step; when and how the institute becomes activated; hand-off points IADM-04 must call or be called by; conflicts with the rule 'PENDING = zero access, access only when institute activated AND subscription is TRIAL or ACTIVE'. No code, database or Git changes.

Story name: Inspect existing billing code, schema and permission gate
User story: As the IADM-04 engineer, I inventory the existing institute-admin billing endpoints, tables, repositories, tests and the platform-admin permission gate, and classify each capability REUSE / MOVE / NEW.
Acceptance criteria: Report covers controllers, services, repositories, tests, tables, RLS (row-level security) policies and permission keys, each classified REUSE / MOVE / NEW with reasons. Existing capability is moved, not copied or rebuilt. Plan for retiring moved monolith routes (410 Gone, same pattern as the IADM-02 cutover) is proposed, not executed.

Story name: Inspect shared audit, IADM-02 policy keys, gateway, claims and usage sources
User story: As the IADM-04 engineer, I confirm what already exists for shared audit, IADM-02 billing/trial/grace policy keys, gateway routing and claims, and usage-producing services.
Acceptance criteria: Report states: whether shared audit gives a durable write that can be awaited before an external call; which IADM-02 keys exist for trial, grace, renewal and billing time zone (missing keys are listed, not invented); gateway prefix/port conventions to follow (the old 8099-8106 plan is NOT assumed); which services could report usage. Nothing is created.

Story name: Contract baseline document for owner review
User story: As the owner, I get a short contract baseline (subscription state machine, access gate, entitlement-check contract, proposed permission-key map, reuse plan) so I can approve before building.
Acceptance criteria: Document covers: states TRIAL, PENDING, ACTIVE, grace, expired, suspended, cancelled and every allowed transition; the dual access gate; entitlement-check request/response; proposed permission keys (marked PROPOSED, nothing assumed verified); IADM-01 contract changes needed (smallest possible). Flags the one-current-subscription rule as PROPOSED, pending owner confirmation.

Story name: DEV demo data pack for plans, institutes and the two Super Admin accounts
User story: As the owner, I can open the desks and see real demo data, not empty lists, including two distinct Super Admin accounts.
Acceptance criteria: DEV only, via the project's existing seed/persona conventions, with rollback script and before/after snapshot. Creates: Demo Institute A and B; plans BASIC, STANDARD, PREMIUM; a trial fixture; Super Admin accounts USR-R01A and USR-R01B (two distinct accounts, same role, no new role); System Admin, Institution Admin (Institute A), College Admin and Auditor demo users. All values labelled DEMO; no production target.

Story name: Super Admin views the plan and package catalogue with versions
User story: As a Super Admin, I can see all plans/packages with version, status and included entitlements, so I know what institutes can subscribe to.
Screen / desk: Platform Subscription Desk: Plan & package catalogue
Acceptance criteria: List and detail screens show demo plans. Allowed: Super Admin. Denied (tested): College Admin; Institution Admin cannot see global catalogue administration. Loading, empty, error, unauthorized states exist. Audit entry for reads is not required.

Story name: Super Admin creates, edits and deprecates plans, packages and pricing
User story: As a Super Admin, I can create, update and deprecate a plan/package and set its price, so the commercial offer is under platform control.
Screen / desk: Platform Subscription Desk: Plan & package catalogue
Acceptance criteria: Create/update/deprecate works end to end on screen and API. Price stored as whole minor units plus currency code; no tax logic. New plan versions do not rewrite existing subscriptions or invoices. Each change writes shared audit. Denied (tested): System Admin, Institution Admin, College Admin, Auditor. Deprecated plan cannot be newly attached.

Story name: Super Admin maps plans to features and quotas
User story: As a Super Admin, I can choose which IADM-02 feature flags each plan includes and set quota values, so entitlements come from the plan.
Acceptance criteria: Mapping uses existing IADM-02 feature-flag definitions (no duplicate flag store). Quota value and unit saved per plan version. Unknown flag is rejected. Audited. Denied (tested) for non-Super-Admin roles.

Story name: Super Admin configures the free-trial policy
User story: As a Super Admin, I can configure trial eligibility, duration, included entitlements/quotas and conversion rules, so trials follow a set policy.
Screen / desk: Platform Subscription Desk: Plan & package catalogue (trial policy)
Acceptance criteria: All trial values are configurable data; no value is hard-coded. Policy is read through the IADM-02 configuration mechanism where it exists (any new keys are registered there and listed in the report). Policy versioned; evaluation deterministic and audited. DEMO values only in seed data.

Story name: Attach a plan or eligible trial to an institute during onboarding
User story: As the onboarding workflow, I can attach a plan or eligible trial to a new institute and get back a TRIAL or PENDING subscription, so billing starts with the institute.
Screen / desk: Onboarding wizard (existing IADM-01 screens, minimal hook)
Acceptance criteria: Eligible trial creates TRIAL with no payment; otherwise creates PENDING with an invoice intent. Same idempotency key returns the same subscription (no duplicates). Unknown/inactive institute or deprecated plan rejected. IADM-04 never activates the institute. Smallest possible change to IADM-01; every change listed in the report.

Story name: One current subscription per institute (TRIAL, PENDING, ACTIVE together)
User story: As the platform, I never allow a second current subscription for an institute while one is TRIAL, PENDING or ACTIVE, so billing and access stay unambiguous.
Acceptance criteria: Enforced in service and database constraint. Second attach attempt is rejected with a clear message. Marked PROPOSED rule pending owner confirmation; easy to change; flagged in the report.

Story name: Super Admin sees subscriptions across institutes
User story: As a Super Admin, I can list and open any institute's subscription with plan, state, term, invoices and history, so I can manage the platform.
Screen / desk: Platform Subscription Desk: Subscription overview and Institute subscription detail
Acceptance criteria: Shows TRIAL, PENDING, ACTIVE and other demo subscriptions with state history. Filter by state. Loading, empty, error states exist. Denied (tested): College Admin; Institution Admin only sees own institute.

Story name: System Admin sees operational billing view only
User story: As a System Admin, I can view the operational billing information I am granted, so I can support the platform without commercial authority.
Acceptance criteria: View-only to start; any operational action is added only with its own permission key (see later stories). Attempts to create/change plans, prices, approvals, refunds or credits are denied and tested. Message shown matches the blueprint wording.

Story name: Institution Admin sees own subscription and renewal state
User story: As an Institution Admin, I can see my institute's current plan, state (trial, pending, active), trial or renewal date, so I know where we stand.
Acceptance criteria: Shows only own institute. Cross-institute access (Institute B) denied and audited. Pending state clearly explains that access is unavailable until payment. College Admin cannot open this desk.

Story name: Institution Admin sees what the plan includes
User story: As an Institution Admin, I can see the features and limits included in my plan, so I know what my institute can use.
Acceptance criteria: Shows features and quota limits for own institute only. PENDING shows none available. Read only.

Story name: Single entitlement-check contract with fail-closed access gate
User story: As a platform or college-side service, I can ask one authenticated contract whether an institute may use a feature, so access follows the subscription.
Acceptance criteria: Grants only when IADM-01 says the institute is activated AND subscription is TRIAL or ACTIVE. PENDING always returns zero entitlements even if the institute is activated. Unknown institute, unknown feature, stale state or unavailable policy returns deny. No unlimited fallback. College Admin gains no billing access. Allowed and denied tests exist.

Story name: Institution Admin requests a plan change
User story: As an Institution Admin, I can request an upgrade or downgrade for my institute, so we can change plans through the proper approval.
Screen / desk: Institution Subscription Desk: Request plan change
Acceptance criteria: Creates a plan-change request (requested plan, effective date, status). Cannot apply it directly. Own institute only. Denied (tested): other institute, College Admin. Audited.

Story name: Super Admin approves or rejects a plan-change request
User story: As a Super Admin, I can approve or reject a plan-change request, and an approved change applies from its effective date only.
Acceptance criteria: Approval applies prospectively; past invoices and pricing snapshots are unchanged. Rejected request records a reason. Denied (tested): System Admin, Institution Admin. Proration and credits are NOT calculated (decision pending); report shows this clearly.

Story name: Generate a subscription invoice with a pricing snapshot
User story: As the billing workflow, I generate an invoice from the approved plan price and keep a snapshot, so invoices can be reproduced later.
Acceptance criteria: Amount stored as whole minor units plus currency code. Pricing snapshot stored with invoice. Stable internal invoice reference; no GST/tax or numbering rules invented (pending Finance decision). Same request twice gives one invoice. Audited.

Story name: Trial conversion: raise invoice and move TRIAL to PENDING
User story: As the platform, when a trial reaches conversion I raise the invoice and move the same subscription to PENDING, so payment is required to continue.
Acceptance criteria: TRIAL to PENDING on the same subscription; invoice raised once (idempotent); PENDING returns zero entitlements immediately. Trial values come from policy, not code. Audited. Manual trigger available for demo; schedule comes in a later story.

Story name: Institution Admin sees own invoices and payment status
User story: As an Institution Admin, I can see my invoices and whether they are paid, so I can follow up on payment.
Acceptance criteria: Own institute only; status shows draft, issued, due, paid, void. Cross-institute denied. Read only.

Story name: Super Admin manages invoices
User story: As a Super Admin, I can generate, view and cancel/void an invoice where policy allows, so billing mistakes can be handled.
Acceptance criteria: Generate, view, void work on screen and API. Void keeps history; nothing is deleted. Refunds and credits are not implemented (decision pending). Denied (tested): System Admin, Institution Admin, Auditor.

Story name: Super Admin records offline payment evidence (account A)
User story: As a Super Admin, I can record bank-transfer or cheque evidence against an invoice, so offline payments are captured.
Screen / desk: Platform Subscription Desk: Payment & reconciliation desk
Acceptance criteria: Creates an offline-payment evidence record (instrument, reference, amount in minor units, currency, recorder, time). Evidence is immutable. Invoice does NOT become paid at this step. Audited.

Story name: A different Super Admin reconciles the offline payment (account B)
User story: As a second Super Admin, I can verify and reconcile the recorded evidence, so an invoice is marked paid only after independent checking.
Screen / desk: Platform Subscription Desk: Payment & reconciliation desk
Acceptance criteria: Reconciliation is a separate record. Same account that recorded it is denied (tested). If only one Super Admin account exists, the workflow is blocked with the blueprint message and no role substitution (tested). On approval the invoice becomes paid.

Story name: Move PENDING to ACTIVE only on verified payment
User story: As the platform, I move a subscription from PENDING to ACTIVE only after verified payment or approved offline reconciliation, so access is never granted on an unconfirmed payment.
Acceptance criteria: Payment initiation alone never activates. Mismatch of amount or currency holds for reconciliation and changes nothing. After ACTIVE, the access gate grants entitlements only if the institute is also activated. Idempotent and audited.

Story name: Payment-provider adapter with a DEV simulator
User story: As the platform, I talk to payments through one adapter interface backed by a clearly labelled DEV simulator, so everything can be demonstrated before a provider is chosen.
Acceptance criteria: No real provider, credentials or network calls. Simulator can produce pending, success, failure, duplicate and invalid-signature outcomes. Invoice/payment intent AND durable audit evidence are saved BEFORE the adapter is called; if audit is unavailable the call is not made (tested). Choosing the real provider is a separate owner decision.

Story name: Super Admin initiates online payment for an invoice
User story: As a Super Admin, I can start an online payment for an invoice and watch its status, so online payments can be collected.
Screen / desk: Platform Subscription Desk: Payment & reconciliation desk
Acceptance criteria: Status shown: pending, confirmed, failed. Initiation is not settlement. Duplicate initiation does not create a second payment. Denied (tested): other roles.

Story name: Signed provider callback route with replay protection
User story: As the platform, I accept payment callbacks on a dedicated route that checks signature, time window and correlation, so only genuine confirmations change billing state.
Acceptance criteria: Dedicated machine ingress, no admin login required. Tests: valid, invalid signature, replayed, duplicate (safely acknowledged, no double settlement), unauthorized source. Invalid callbacks change nothing and leave security evidence. IP allow-list only if available.

Story name: Super Admin reconciles mismatched or unmatched online payments
User story: As a Super Admin, I can review and resolve unmatched or mismatched online payments, so the books agree with the provider.
Screen / desk: Platform Subscription Desk: Payment & reconciliation desk
Acceptance criteria: Lists unmatched, mismatched, duplicate and failed payments with reasons. Resolution recorded with evidence and audited. Auditor and System Admin cannot resolve (tested).

Story name: System Admin inspects and retries failed callbacks
User story: As a System Admin, I can inspect integration failures and retry a failed callback, so technical problems are fixed without commercial authority.
Acceptance criteria: Only these allow-listed actions are permitted. Retry is idempotent. Creating or changing plans, prices, approvals, refunds or credits stays denied (tested).

Story name: Scheduled renewal, trial-conversion and expiry jobs
User story: As the platform, I run renewal reminders, trial conversion and expiry as scheduled jobs under a dedicated service identity, so lifecycle changes happen on time.
Acceptance criteria: Jobs are idempotent, checkpointed and safe to retry; they use a narrowly scoped service permission, not a human role. Grace, renewal and expiry values come from IADM-02 policy. Billing time zone and expiry-day boundary are read from configuration; if not configured, expiry jobs do not run (fail closed). Nothing is assumed from server locale or India time.

Story name: Super Admin reviews and handles renewals and expiries
User story: As a Super Admin, I can see upcoming renewals and expiries and act on them under policy, so subscriptions do not lapse by accident.
Screen / desk: Platform Subscription Desk: Renewal & expiry desk
Acceptance criteria: Shows due, grace, renewed, expired, suspended with dates. Renewal applies only after payment checks. Expiry follows policy. Audited. Denied (tested): other roles.

Story name: Record usage measurements idempotently against plan quotas
User story: As a platform service, I can report usage for an institute so quota consumption is tracked.
Acceptance criteria: Each measurement has source, period, unit and deduplication key; duplicates are ignored. Stale or unavailable source is marked incomplete, never invented. No overage charge and no automatic throttling. Tenant isolated.

Story name: Institution Admin sees usage against quota
User story: As an Institution Admin, I can see how much of each plan limit my institute has used, so I can plan an upgrade.
Acceptance criteria: Own institute only; shows used vs limit, period, and an 'incomplete data' note when a source is stale. Read only.

Story name: Scoped billing reports
User story: As an authorized user, I can view billing summaries within my scope, so I can follow billing health.
Screen / desk: Billing reports (platform, institute and audit views)
Acceptance criteria: Super Admin: platform-wide. Institution Admin: own institute only. Auditor: assigned scope, read only. College Admin denied. Export, if any, respects the same scope.

Story name: Auditor inspects billing evidence read-only
User story: As an Auditor, I can read invoices, subscription history, payment references, reconciliation outcomes and audit evidence in my scope, without any way to change them.
Acceptance criteria: Every mutation control is absent on screen and denied at API (tested headed in the browser, not only by API).

Story name: Verify tenant isolation and role denials
User story: As a security owner, I can see proof that Institution Admins cannot reach other institutes and College Admins have no billing access.
Acceptance criteria: Allowed and denied test report across Super Admin, System Admin, Institution Admin (own and other institute), College Admin, Auditor: gateway, service, database row-level security and screen. Service-identity checks included.

Story name: Verify audit trace and audit/notification outage behaviour
User story: As an operator, I can trace an invoice, payment intent, callback and subscription change end to end in shared audit, and I can see the system behave correctly when audit or notifications are down.
Acceptance criteria: Trace shown for one full onboarding-to-ACTIVE flow. With audit disabled, no financial change reports success and the provider is not called. With notifications disabled, billing state is unchanged and notice is delayed. Outage runs are demonstrated, not just coded.
Owner notes / status: partially completed — durable audit present; full outage demo deferred

Story name: Verify student fees stay in the Finance domain
User story: As the platform owner, I can see proof that no student-fee route, table or data path exists in IADM-04 and no invoice-summary sync to FIN exists.
Acceptance criteria: Route, repository and dependency scan documented. No FIN integration code present.

Story name: Final evidence pack and move/retire report
User story: As the owner, I get one evidence pack showing each story's API, screen and demo status with real proof, and the plan for retiring moved monolith billing routes.
Acceptance criteria: Per story: API-ready, Screen-ready, Demo-verified with evidence (headed browser run results/screenshots/video using the project's existing setup, test reports, audit evidence). Stories without proof stay unchecked. Retirement of old routes proposed with the same 410 pattern; executed only after the new route is demo-verified and the owner agrees.
